core_obligations: Reduction (proof lines 499-505): a nonsingular projective model X' of X shares a nonempty open with X, so X' is geometrically irreducible as X is (small birational-invariance detail omitted); hence one may assume X proper for part (2)'s input.

Part (1) (proof lines 507-518): for X proper, X_K is proper, its normalization is finite over it hence proper, and being normal, irreducible and birational to (X_K)_red it is the unique nonsingular projective model.

Part (2) (proof lines 520-528): the finite purely inseparable extension making the model geometrically normal exists by the normalization lemma; for curves normal equals regular, and geometrically regular implies smooth.
Parts (3) and (4) (proof lines 530-535): geometrically reduced proper varieties have H^0 = K, and smooth base changes are smooth, so the model commutes with further extension Omega.
proof_roadmap: Use the birational invariance of geometric irreducibility to reduce to the proper case.
Prove uniqueness of the model over K by properness of the normalization.
Construct the purely inseparable field extension that makes the model smooth.
Read off H^0 = K from geometric reducedness and compatibility with base change from smoothness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four functorial properties of nonsingular projective models under field extension (statement lines 478-497). The proof (lines 499-535) is a four-part reference chain: birational reduction to the proper case (with a small birational-invariance detail the author marks omitted), properness of normalizations for (1), the purely inseparable improvement argument normal-regular-smooth for (2), and global-section plus base-change arguments for (3) and (4). The single omitted detail sits in the auxiliary reduction, not in any of the four conclusions. H2: standard assembly of earlier results with correctly ordered hinges.
